## ACS Data

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
education <- vroom(here("data", "education.csv"))
employment <- vroom(here("data", "employment.csv"))
ethnicity <- vroom(here("data", "ethnicity.csv"))
median_income <- vroom(here("data", "median_income.csv"))
population <- vroom(here("data", "population.csv"))

cleaning_ACS <- function(df){
  names(df)[2:ncol(df)] <- as.character(df[1, 2:ncol(df)])
  df <- df[-1, ] #explicit title is in line 1
  df <- df[, -ncol(df)] #always full of NA
  df[3:ncol(df)] <- lapply(df[3:ncol(df)], as.integer) #integer type for every column but 1 & 2
  df
}

education <- cleaning_ACS(education)
employment <- cleaning_ACS(employment)
ethnicity <- cleaning_ACS(ethnicity) |>
  select(!4) #full of NA
median_income <- cleaning_ACS(median_income)
population <- cleaning_ACS(population) |>
  select(!4) #full of NA
```

# Data joining and cleaning

## Separating state and county in ACS Data

In order to join the data, it is essential first to work with our key variable under the same format.

### Harmonizing State and County's name format

In EPA Data, we have two different columns County Name and State Name. In ACS Data, we have one unique column under the following form : County Name, State Name. We then have to split them by "," to obtain two different columns, in order to have the same form in both datasets. 

```{r}
sep_state_county_str <- function(df){
  df |> 
    separate_wider_delim(`Geographic Area Name`,
                         delim = ",",
                         names = c("County Name", "State Name"))
}

remove_county_suffix <- function(df){
  df$`County Name` <- str_remove(df$`County Name`, " County$")
  df
}
#$ sert à enlever " County" en fin de chaîne uniquement (plus sûr)

education <- education |>
  sep_state_county_str() |>
  remove_county_suffix()
employment <- employment |>
  sep_state_county_str() |>
  remove_county_suffix()
ethnicity <- ethnicity |>
  sep_state_county_str() |>
  remove_county_suffix()
median_income <- median_income |>
  sep_state_county_str() |>
  remove_county_suffix()
population <- population |>
  sep_state_county_str() |>
  remove_county_suffix()
```

### Harmonizing State and County's code format

In EPA Data, we have a State code and a County Code (1, 24 or 456 for instance). In ACS Data we have a unique geo_id where the five last numbers are the State code and the County Code in that order. Therefore, we have to extract these last 5 numbers from the geo_id, to split them and to turn 001 into 1 for instance. After mutating, we will have two new columns, one County Code and one State Code, with numbers as 1, 24 or 456 for instance : the format will be exactly the same between the two datasets.

```{r}
sep_county_state_code <- function(df){
  df |>
    mutate(`State Code` = as.integer(str_sub(GEO_ID, -5, -4)),
           `County Code` = as.integer(str_sub(GEO_ID, -3, -1)))
}
#-5 est le 5ème élément du geo_id en partant de la fin
#as.integer transforms 001 into 1 for instance

education <- sep_county_state_code(education)
employment <- sep_county_state_code(employment)
ethnicity <- sep_county_state_code(ethnicity)
median_income <- sep_county_state_code(median_income)
population <- sep_county_state_code(population)
```
